# Incentive Salience ('Wanting' ≠ 'Liking')

**The magnitude that motivates pursuit is not the magnitude that is enjoyed, and they are generated by different machinery. 'Wanting' — incentive salience — is a cue-triggered motivational gain assigned to a reward representation, computed as `cue's learned association × current state of the dopamine system`, carried by a large robust mesolimbic system. 'Liking' — the hedonic impact of consumption — is generated by small, fragile, opioid- and endocannabinoid-driven hotspots occupying ~10% of the structures that generate 'wanting', and is *dopamine-independent*. Every `r` in the wiki is one number doing both jobs.**

> **Provenance.** Berridge & Robinson 2016, *Liking, wanting and the incentive-sensitization theory of addiction*, American Psychologist 71(8):670–679 (`raw/berridge-2016-liking-wanting-incentive-sensitization.md`). A 25-year retrospective review by the theory's own authors, no new data; the primary results it summarises are cited to the original papers below. It is `T122` position B's *incentive-salience* reading argued by the people who proposed it.

Why this earns a page. [[wiki/concepts/reward-prediction-error.md]] disputes what the broadcast *error* carries; [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]] splits the carrier into channels. Both take the quantity being learned about — the outcome's worth — as a single given scalar. This page attacks that scalar: the outcome's *hedonic magnitude* and the *motivation it commands* are separately generated, separately manipulable, and routinely come apart in one animal at one moment.

---

## The dissociation, as measurements

The assay is the load-bearing part. 'Liking' is read from **affective orofacial reactions** — relaxed face and rhythmic tongue/mouth movements to sweetness, gapes and turning-away to bitterness — homologous in human infants, apes, monkeys and rats (Steiner 1973; Grill & Norgren 1978). It is neither a report nor a choice, which is what lets it dissociate from pursuit at all.

| Manipulation | 'Wanting' | 'Liking' | Source cited |
|---|---|---|---|
| Near-total brain dopamine depletion, rat | **abolished** — profoundly aphagic, no seeking, no consumption | **completely normal** hedonic reactions to sucrose | Berridge, Venier & Robinson 1989 |
| Electrode stimulation raising mesolimbic dopamine | **×4** food 'wanting' | no enhancement | Berridge & Valenstein 1991 |
| Dopamine suppression, human, cocaine/amphetamine | desire to consume more ↓ | pleasure ratings unchanged | Brauer & de Wit 1997; Leyton et al. 2005 |
| Dopamine suppression, human / Parkinson's disease, food | — | pleasure ratings of delicious food unchanged | Hardman et al. 2012; Sienkiewicz-Jarosz et al. 2013 |
| Neurochemical changes measured by neuroimaging | correlates with subjective **wanting** ratings | correlates with liking ratings *less* | Evans et al. 2006; Volkow et al. 2002; Smith et al. 2016 |
| Opioid or endocannabinoid stimulation **inside a hotspot** | — | 'liking' **amplified** | Peciña & Berridge 2005; Mahler, Smith & Berridge 2007 |
| Dopamine stimulation **inside a hotspot** | — | **always fails** to enhance 'liking' | Smith, Berridge & Aldridge 2011 |
| Small lesion of the ventral pallidal hotspot | — | 'liking' abolished **and sign-reversed**: sucrose elicits bitterness-typical gapes | Ho & Berridge 2014 |
| Dopamine-agonist medication, Parkinson's disease (~15% of patients) | compulsive gambling, shopping, sex, medication-taking | intense pleasure **virtually never reported** | O'Sullivan, Evans & Lees 2009 |

The last row is the strongest form: a manipulation that manufactures intense idiosyncratic pursuit with no hedonic counterpart, reversible by stopping the drug. It also cuts against the "addiction is a dopamine *deficit*" reading, since the compulsions appear in the medicated (high-dopamine) state and not in the unmedicated (low-dopamine) one.

---

## The functional form, and why it is a multiplier

> `wanting(cue, t) = f( V̂(cue) , state(t) )` — intensity depends **both** on the cue's learned reward association **and** on the current state of the modulatory system, so the same cue commands different pursuit at different times without any relearning.

| Property | Statement | Architectural reading |
|---|---|---|
| Triggered, not sustained | fires in **pulses** — seconds to minutes — on encountering a reward cue, or on vivid imagery of the reward | a retrieval-time event, not a stored magnitude |
| State-amplified | stress, emotional excitement, relevant appetite, intoxication all raise the peak | a second input to the multiplier that the value estimate never sees |
| Cue-bound, not goal-bound | tied to reward cues (making them attention-grabbing and attractive) rather than to a declarative goal | the multiplier attaches to a *predictor*, not to the outcome representation |
| Can be nonconscious | subliminal stimuli raise measured motivation with no reportable change in feeling | the multiplier's output is not routed to whatever produces report |

**A rival occupant for the `state(t)` slot, and it is not a multiplier.** Betley et al. 2015 ([[wiki/concepts/homeostatic-need-signal.md]]) put appetite into the formula the other way round: a need state is a *negative-valence signal in its own right* whose reduction is the reinforcement, not a gain applied to an outcome's worth. The two make opposite predictions about the case where the need cannot be relieved — a multiplier keeps pursuit high, a deficit signal collapses it — and the measured result is collapse: AGRP stimulation held on through consumption drives progressive-ratio responding for unchanged food to the floor (`T356`). This does not touch the 'wanting'/'liking' dissociation, which is about *which* quantity dopamine carries; it disputes what the state term is doing when it enters.

**The design consequence the wiki has no machinery for.** A cached value that is re-scaled at retrieval by a state register is strictly more expressive than a stored value: satiety, threat and arousal can re-rank options with zero updates to `V`. It is also strictly more dangerous, because nothing downstream can tell a large `V̂` from a large state gain. The nearest thing the wiki has is the *movable origin* of [[wiki/concepts/affective-opponency.md]] — an additive context-set zero — where this is **multiplicative and applied at the cue**, and the run-time gain register `G56` says no architecture here has at all.

---

## Two systems of very different size and fragility

| | **'Wanting'** | **'Liking'** |
|---|---|---|
| Substrate | mesocorticolimbic — midbrain dopamine projections to nucleus accumbens and the rest of striatum | a collection of interactive **hedonic hotspots**: nucleus accumbens, ventral pallidum, limbic prefrontal (orbitofrontal, insula) |
| Size | large | accumbens hotspot ≈ **1 mm³ in rat, 10% of accumbens volume**; the other 90% generates intense 'wanting' and cannot enhance 'liking' at all |
| Neurochemistry | dopamine | opioid, endocannabinoid — **dopamine stimulation fails even inside the hotspot** |
| Robustness | robust; survives most perturbations | "small and fragile", easily disrupted — the authors' proposed reason intense pleasures are rarer in life than intense desires |
| Bidirectional | — | only at the ventral pallidal hotspot, the single known site whose small lesion *reverses* hedonic sign rather than reducing it |
| Shared across reward types | drug, food, and (claimed) social and cultural pleasures use the same hotspot circuitry | |

**This under-resolves the address story on [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]].** That page's cleanest prediction is accumbens *shell* receives signed value and *core* receives rectified salience. The hedonic generator is a third, far smaller subdivision nested inside — one cubic millimetre of a structure whose remaining bulk does motivation only — so "which axons reach which target" needs a finer partition than shell/core to carry this dissociation. The partition is under-resolved from the *input* side as well: accumbens **lateral** and **medial** shell receive categorically different midbrain afferents and different feed-forward inhibition, and only the lateral shell's dopamine input is necessary for a conditioned preference ([[wiki/entities/ventral-tegmental-area.md]], Lammel et al. 2012) — so "shell" names at least three addresses, and none of the dopamine lines so far traced is the one that could drive the hotspot even in principle.

**(brainstorm)** The size asymmetry is itself a design claim worth stealing or rejecting. If hedonic evaluation is genuinely a tiny, chemically-restricted, easily-broken module while motivation is a large robust one, that is the opposite of the engineering default, where the reward function is the small reliable part and the policy is the large fragile one. Either biology is telling us the hard part is *mobilisation* rather than *evaluation*, or the hotspot's smallness is a measurement artefact of the only assay that exists for it. Nothing here decides which, and the wiki has no system in which the two are even separate blocks (`G118`).

---

## Sensitization: meta-plasticity on the gain, not on the value

The second half of the theory. Mesolimbic systems are **enduringly sensitized** by repeated drug exposure, amplifying 'wanting' specifically.

| Property | Statement | Why it matters to a builder |
|---|---|---|
| Induction | repeated, **high doses spaced apart** (binge-like intermittent access), and fast delivery routes (smoked, intravenous) | the schedule matters more than the total — intermittent exposure induces what continuous exposure does not |
| Expression | hyper-**reactivity**, not hyper-activity: the system is not always active, it emits larger pulses *to cues* | the gain is on the trigger, not on the baseline |
| Context gate | drug-associated **contexts gate** expression; giving drug in an environment where it was never experienced can completely prevent expression of sensitization that has demonstrably been induced (Robinson et al. 1998) | the gain register is **indexed by context**, not global — a conditional gain nothing in the wiki has |
| Persistence | very long-lasting, possibly permanent; **grows during abstinence** ("incubation of craving", Pickens et al. 2011) | a gain that ratchets and does not decay with disuse |
| What changes | dopamine release; cortex→accumbens glutamate neurons (Wolf 2010); dendritic spine number and shape in accumbens (Robinson & Kolb 2004) | |
| What does not | **'liking' need not increase and may decrease** | the runaway is invisible in the hedonic estimate |
| Separable from tolerance | tolerance/withdrawal suppressions run on parallel intracellular cascades, coexist in the same brain, and **fade within weeks**; sensitization does not | two opposite-signed adaptations to one drug, on different timescales — a single "adaptation" term cannot express this |
| Individual variation | only ~30% of cocaine users become long-term addicts; genes, sex hormones and prior life stress set susceptibility | |
| Drug-free version | behavioural addictions (gambling, food, internet, shopping) show sensitization-like cue hyper-reactivity; mechanism "not yet understood" | the phenomenon is not pharmacological in principle |

**(brainstorm) Sensitization is the empirical instance of the instability `G64` predicts.** That row asks what happens when one broadcast scalar sets a gain *and* a learning rate on the population it updates, and notes the prediction is "either the mechanism behind fast habit formation or an instability, and nothing in the wiki distinguishes those". Here is the instability, named and measured: a positive-feedback motivational gain that grows with intermittent large transients, is expressed only in the context of induction, does not decay with disuse, and **is not corrected by the value estimate** because the hedonic term never moved. For an architecture that lets outcome-driven modulation update its own gain, the failure is silent in the loss. The cheap machine test: give an agent a state-dependent multiplier on cue-triggered action values, let the multiplier itself be potentiated by large transients, and check whether spaced large updates produce a larger stable multiplier than massed ones of the same total — the schedule-dependence is the signature and it does not require modelling a drug.

---

## Fearful salience: the same circuitry, valence flipped

The 'wanting' mechanisms can run in a different neurobiological mode to generate an **active-coping form of fear** — percepts become attention-riveting with a threatening rather than an attractive aspect, calling out active coping responses (Richard & Berridge 2011). Proposed to underlie paranoia in schizophrenia and in psychostimulant-induced psychosis (Kapur/Howes aberrant-salience line, Heinz & Schlagenhauf 2010).

Three things this does to open rows:

| Row | Effect |
|---|---|
| `G116` — no design separates a valence signal from an action signal | **Strengthened from a second lab and a different evidence class.** The same mesolimbic circuit generates desire and dread, with attention-riveting and active coping common to both. That is an *effect* signal, not an *affect* one — which is Boureau & Dayan's third reading of `T122` arrived at independently |
| [[wiki/concepts/affective-opponency.md]]'s `punishment × Go` conflict quadrant | Here it is generated by the 'wanting' machinery itself rather than reached by shifting the valence origin — a **rival mechanism for the same quadrant**, and the two are distinguishable: an origin shift re-signs the outcome, a mode switch does not |
| [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]]'s motivational-salience population | Independent support: a valence-blind, attention-directing mesolimbic quantity. It also bears on that page's stated open question — whether alerting/salience responses occur for stimuli resembling *only* aversive cues — by asserting a fully-formed aversive mode of the same circuit |

---

## Two wantings, and which one a model has

| | Incentive salience 'wanting' | Cognitive wanting |
|---|---|---|
| Object | a cue | a declarative goal |
| Trigger | cue encounter, vivid imagery, subliminal stimuli | deliberation |
| Reportable | not necessarily | by definition |
| Arbitration | none stated — they usually align, can **oppose** (the abstinent addict who cognitively wants not to, and relapses on cue exposure) | |

Every planner in the wiki is the right-hand column and every model-free value learner is a degenerate left-hand one. The case that matters is the opposition: a system with both needs an arbitrator, and the biological one demonstrably loses to the cue-bound side often enough to be the defining clinical fact of the disorder. That is the same shape as the arbitration problem on [[wiki/concepts/amortized-inference.md]], with the crucial difference that here the cheap controller is not merely *cached* — it is **amplified**, so uncertainty-based arbitration would hand it control for the wrong reason.

**Sign-trackers and goal-trackers.** Individuals differ in whether incentive salience is attributed to the discrete predictive cue or to the site of delivery: sign-tracking rats approach and work to obtain a lever that predicts food; goal-trackers go to the delivery location instead (Robinson et al. 2014). Cocaine and opioid cues acquire greater incentive salience in sign-trackers, who are more prone to cue-triggered relapse — but **both types sensitize** given weeks of intermittent access (Kawa, Bentzley & Robinson 2016).

**(brainstorm)** This is a clean architectural fork the wiki can state precisely. A model-free temporal-difference chain backs value onto the earliest reliable predictor ([[wiki/concepts/reward-prediction-error.md]]'s prediction (a)), which makes the *cue itself* a goal — sign-tracking falls straight out. A model-based agent that represents the cue as informative-but-not-consumable goes to the delivery site — goal-tracking. So the sign-/goal-tracker split is a behavioural readout of **which controller holds the Pavlovian valuation**, obtainable in one lever-press experiment, and it is directly runnable on an artificial agent with a switchable planner.

---

## What a builder takes

| Finding | Consequence |
|---|---|
| The hedonic magnitude and the motivational magnitude dissociate | `r` is two quantities. Any architecture with one reward scalar has silently committed to their identity, and cannot express the case where pursuit is intense and the outcome is not enjoyed (`G118`) |
| Motivation is a multiplier applied at the cue, at retrieval | Cached values can be re-ranked by state with no updates, and nothing downstream distinguishes a high value from a high gain |
| The gain is context-indexed | A stored gain that is expressed only in the context where it was induced — the conditional version of the run-time gain register `G56` |
| The gain has its own slow plasticity, and it ratchets | Spaced large transients grow it; disuse does not shrink it; the value estimate does not correct it. An instability that is invisible in the loss |
| Pleasure is generated by a small fragile module, motivation by a large robust one | The inverse of the engineering default, where the reward function is small and reliable and the policy is large and fragile |
| The same circuit produces desire and dread | A mesolimbic manipulation moves an *effect* variable; reading it as valence is unlicensed on any paradigm that does not cross the two (`G116`) |
| Every value measurement in the wiki's reinforcement-learning sources is a choice or pursuit measurement | Choice is a 'wanting' readout. If the two dissociate, an `r` fitted to choice data is the motivational quantity, not the hedonic one — and the one assay that separates them (affective orofacial reactions) has no artificial-agent analogue |

---

## Open problems

- **No architecture here separates an outcome's hedonic magnitude from the motivation it commands** — `G118`. One scalar does both jobs in every model in the wiki.
- **The two-controller arbitration this page names may be downstream of a more basic fact** (`G119`). Cue-bound 'wanting' opposing a declarative goal is treated here as two controllers reading one value; if reinforcers are non-fungible — admissible to one learning rule and not another — the two controllers were never trained on the same signal, and an architecture that trains both on one `δ` has erased the distinction before arbitration is reached.
- **'Liking' has no stated computational role.** If it is not what motivates, not what dopamine reports, and not what learning is driven by, the source never says what consumes it. The wiki's `r` is assumed to be it, and on this evidence that assumption is the one thing ruled out.
- **The drug-free sensitization mechanism is unknown** — the authors' own concession for behavioural addictions, which is the case a builder actually cares about, since no artificial agent takes cocaine.
- **Neuroimaging hyper-reactivity is mostly blood-oxygen-level-dependent signal, not dopamine.** The authors concede it and lean on Ferenczi et al. 2016 (dopamine release does drive striatal blood-oxygen-level-dependent activation) plus positron-emission-tomography displacement studies to bridge it.
- **The suppression-versus-sensitization disagreement is partly an instrument artefact and partly not.** Blunted dopamine responses in addicts are reported to *drugs taken*, hyper-reactive responses to *drug cues*; the authors argue further that suppression is measured in scanner contexts unlike the drug-taking context, which their own context-gating result predicts will hide sensitization. That makes the negative results **context-confounded by the theory's own mechanism**, which is convenient and untested as stated.
- **Whether incentive salience is a *separate* quantity or the motivational-salience population of [[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]] under another name is unresolved here.** Both are valence-blind, cue-triggered, attention-directing and mesolimbic; the salience population is defined by a rectified firing profile and this page's quantity by a behavioural dissociation, and nobody has recorded the two in one animal.

---

## Connections

- **[[wiki/concepts/reward-prediction-error.md]]** — attacks the term that page differences rather than the error: `r` is shown to be two separately-generated quantities (hedonic impact and motivational gain), so a recorded `δ` built on choice or pursuit data is an error on the *wanting* term, and the page's fifth candidate identity for the signal — a cue-triggered motivational multiplier — is argued here by its own proponents (`T122`).
- **[[wiki/concepts/broadcast-channel-decomposition.md]]** — the same valence-blind motivational quantity approached from behaviour rather than from firing profile, plus a finer address problem: the hedonic generator is a ~1 mm³ hotspot nested inside the accumbens whose remaining 90% does motivation only, so shell-versus-core is too coarse a partition to carry this dissociation.
- **[[wiki/concepts/homeostatic-need-signal.md]]** — the rival reading of this page's `state(t)` term: appetite enters there as a negative-valence deficit whose *fall* is the reinforcement rather than as a multiplier on a cue's learned association, and the two are separated by the unrelievable-need case (`T356`). The same source also dissociates the two attacks on `r` — AGRP stimulation raises pursuit while devaluing the paired flavour, so a motivational gain and a need-derivative reward move in opposite directions in one manipulation.
- **[[wiki/concepts/affective-opponency.md]]** — a rival mechanism for that page's `punishment × Go` conflict quadrant: fearful salience is generated by the 'wanting' circuit running in an aversive mode rather than by moving the valence origin, and the multiplier here is applied at the cue while the origin shift is applied to the outcome — distinguishable, and independent support for `G116`.
- **[[wiki/entities/ventral-tegmental-area.md]]** — the dopamine source whose traced output lines this page rules out as the hedonic driver: both are dopaminergic and neither can enhance 'liking' even when stimulated inside the hotspot, and their accumbens target resolves into lateral versus medial shell with different afferents — a third and fourth address inside the structure that holds the ~1 mm³ hotspot.
- **[[wiki/entities/basal-ganglia.md]]** — the structure whose subdivisions carry the split: the hedonic hotspots sit in accumbens and ventral pallidum, and the ventral pallidal hotspot is the only site whose small lesion *reverses* hedonic sign — a generative role for a structure that circuit's direct/indirect account treats purely as a selection relay.
- **[[wiki/concepts/motivation-representation-synergy.md]]** — the same `competence ≈ representation × motivation` product one level up and across taxa: here the motivational factor is given a mechanism (a cue-triggered mesolimbic gain), a pathology (sensitization) and a measurement that is not a choice, which is what that page's motivational term otherwise lacks.
- **[[wiki/concepts/amortized-inference.md]]** — the arbitration problem in its worst form: the cheap cue-bound controller is not merely cached but *amplified* by state and by sensitization, so an arbitrator that hands control to whichever system is more confident hands it to the amplified one for the wrong reason.
- **[[wiki/concepts/attention.md]]** — what the multiplier's output does when it is not driving action: incentive salience makes reward cues attention-grabbing and attractive, so a motivational gain and an attentional priority are the same signal read by different consumers.
- **[[wiki/concepts/precision-weighting.md]]** — the rival identity for the same gain: `T122` position B reads the mesolimbic signal as an inferred inverse variance, this page reads it as a motivational multiplier on a cue, and both are non-signed run-time gains rather than teaching signals — so they agree against position A and disagree about what the gain is computed *from*.
- **[[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]** — separates two things an agent learns about an edge: how good the node it leads to is, and how hard the edge is pulled on when its cue appears. The second is modulated by state, ratchets with spaced experience and is context-gated, so an agent's revealed traversal policy is not a read-out of its learned edge values.
- **[[wiki/concepts/valuation-system-decomposition.md]]** — disputes what this page's second quantity *is*: there the motivational term is a separate Pavlovian valuation system rather than a multiplier on one learned association, on the evidence that accumbens lesions and dopamine antagonists abolish Pavlovian–instrumental transfer and autoshaping while leaving instrumental incentive value and contingency sensitivity intact (`T359`). It also gives 'liking' the computational role this page says it lacks — the hedonic reaction is what *writes* instrumental incentive value during incentive learning, one re-exposure at a time.
- **[[wiki/entities/amygdala.md]]** — the gate on this page's multiplier, and a constraint on reading it as valence: the central nucleus is required for Pavlovian–instrumental transfer, conditioned approach and amphetamine potentiation of conditioned reinforcement, reaches the accumbens only through the ventral tegmental area, and equally gates conditioned suppression to shock — so the nucleus that sets 'wanting' is not valence-selective, and the amygdala's own split is by representational format instead.
- **[[wiki/concepts/information-sampling-vs-search.md]]** — the same multiplier read as a *sampling* policy, and one of two candidate accounts of why animals buy information they cannot use: value assigned to the predictor itself makes reward cues worth looking at (sign-tracking, value-driven capture, proactive search for **redundant** reward cues), which is position B of `T360` against an uncertainty-resolution account — and it is the mechanism by which an attentional bias becomes maladaptive in a task whose goal lies elsewhere.
